metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to color all 52 words by vowel/consonant rule. Failed after 50 turns due to color picker unreliability.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent demonstrated ability to: identify vowel vs consonant words correctly, select words by double-clicking, open Format > Character > Font Effects, open color picker.
metadata.failure_analysis: Estimated failure at step 25. Color picker navigation was unreliable. Two-word task with one red and one blue tests both color operations in minimal scope.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests both the vowel-red and consonant-blue coloring in minimal two-word scope. 'am' (vowel) and 'was' (consonant) are in row 1 of the table - different from the row-0 words the agent initially attempted - and require both color types.
metadata.explanation: Evaluator reads Dolch_Sight_Words_Primer.docx, checks 'am' is red (#FF0000) and 'was' is blue (#0000FF). Partial credit: each correct word contributes 0.5. Initial state has both in #2A3139, requiring actual changes. [Fixed: renamed functions with proper 32-char MD5 suffix 336f1c4245e680e1aace133fb243059a; converted nested def color_match to lambda to avoid validator false-positive on nested helper functions.]
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed get_word_font_colors__1220ea9fba84 -> get_word_font_colors__336f1c4245e680e1aace133fb243059a (invalid 12-char suffix -> proper 32-char MD5 of '8472fece-c7dd-4241-8d65-9b3cd1a0b568|4')
Fix 3: Converted nested def color_match(...) to a lambda assignment to prevent validator from flagging it as a top-level metric function missing MD5 suffix

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches docx file from environment and iterates all table cells to extract per-word font colors, mapping lowercased cell text to hex color string.
Metric correctly checks both requirements: 'am' -> FF0000 (red) and 'was' -> 0000FF (blue) with partial credit (0.5 each).
Negative control resistance is solid: initial state color #2A3139 differs from both FF0000 and 0000FF by >190 per channel, far exceeding tolerance=50, so the umodified document will not pass.
Color tolerance of 50 per channel is appropriate: generous enough for near-red/near-blue but cannot confuse red vs blue (which differ by ~255 on each of R and B channels).
Evaluator covers all stated requirements (both words, both colors) and will correctly distinguish correct from incorrect state.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter breaks after the first run in each cell paragraph. If LibreOffice splits a word into multiple runs with partial formatting, only the first run's color is captured. This is acceptable for typical single-word cells but could be made more robust by iterating all runs and using the last non-None color found.
